conventions.names: R8: device d (1-based, in the order of `devices`) gets as its k-th fresh writer name 8 hex digits of d then 8 of k.
conventions.devices: init: 'new' (nothing stored: catalog defaults), 'empty' (every field stored with no bullets and an empty seen map), {legacy: {field: text}} (DS-UPGRADE), {state: {field: {bullets, seen}}} (stored; the built-in skeleton), 'later' (created by copy), 'shared' (a second process on `store`'s store). catalogExtra: entries this device's catalog has more.
conventions.messages: Each snapshot a device sends is '<device>:<field>#<k>', k counting that device's snapshots of that field from 1. Recipients are the devices connected when it is sent, the sender aside. 'deliver' and 'drop' take `to` (default: every pending recipient) and `parts` (default: every part, in order). 'quiesce' delivers every pending part, oldest first, until none is left (more than 100000 deliveries fails the scenario). 'disconnect' drops what is pending to the device; 'restart' disconnects it, and a fresh process opens the same store.
conventions.expect: live: the exact set of [section, text, name, n]; texts: the exact set of [section, text]; has/lacks: each [section, text] live or not; seen: the exact full seen map. expect_sent counts snapshots of the field the device has sent; expect_quiet: nothing pending.
conventions.fields: A scenario runs on a platform that syncs every field it lists and has every capability in `requires`.

part 2 with a seen key that is not a name
a part number above the part count

scenarios.note: A part whose sender or snap is not a JSON string fails DS-VALIDATE and is dropped; it discards nothing buffered (R19 does not apply). A part with a snap that is not a string, between two valid parts of one snapshot, leaves that snapshot to complete. The control merges.
